newsitem.title: CHINA: China shares seen unshaken by centralisation move.
newsitem.headline: China shares seen unshaken by centralisation move.

text.p: Share prices in China are not expected to react sharply in the wake of Beijing's announcement on Friday that the country's two exchanges will be brought under the direct control of the top securities watchdog, analysts said.
China's State Council ordered the China Securities Regulatory Commission to take direct control of the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges, state media said.

"The move will help strengthen supervision of the stock exchanges but investors do not care much about who will be in charge of the stock exchanges," said an analyst with a major Chinese securities house.
"Rumours about a change in the management system of the stock exchanges have been circulating on the market for some time and have largely been digested," said a second analyst.
Analysts said the move was an indication that central authorities were disappointed with efforts introduced in the middle of the year to cool the overheated exchanges.
The stock markets surged twice between April and December 1996 and in the first four months of 1997, with values soaring more than 50 percent in the first five months of this year.
"The local governments were unable to cool the rampant share fever," an executive with a Chinese brokerage said.
